## 3. Statutes & Legal Frameworks Handled
- Code of Civil Procedure 1908 (CPC): Section 96 (First Appeals), Section 100 (Second Appeals), Section 115 (Civil Revision), Order 39 Rules 1 & 2 (Injunctions), Order 26 (Commissions), Order 7 Rule 11 (Rejection of Plaint), Order 21 (Execution Proceedings).
- Constitution of India: Article 226 (Writ Jurisdiction: Mandamus, Certiorari, Prohibition), Article 227 (High Court Supervisory Jurisdiction over subordinate courts).
- Specific Relief Act 1963: Section 34 (Declaratory Decrees), Section 36-42 (Injunctions), Section 10-20 (Specific Performance of Agreement for Sale).
- Transfer of Property Act 1882: Section 52 (Lis Pendens), Section 53A (Part Performance), Section 54 (Sale), Section 105-111 (Lease and Eviction), Section 106 Notice.
- Indian Succession Act 1925 & Hindu Succession Act 1956: Probate of Wills, Letters of Administration, Succession Certificates, Partition of Coparcenary and Ancestral Property.
- West Bengal Land Reforms Act 1955 (WBLR Act): Section 14 (Vesting & Ceilings), Section 21B (Bargadar Protections), Section 50/51 (Record of Rights, Porcha correction, Mutation).
- Limitation Act 1963: Article 64 & 65 (Possession on basis of title and adverse possession), Section 5 (Condonation of Delay in Appeals).

## 4. Frequently Asked Questions
Q: Can a Second Appeal be filed on questions of fact?
A: No. Under Section 100 of the Code of Civil Procedure 1908, a Second Appeal before the High Court at Calcutta is maintainable only if the High Court is satisfied that the case involves a "Substantial Question of Law". Factual reappraisal is confined to trial and first appellate courts, unless findings are perverse or unsupported by evidence.

Q: What documents are necessary for a property dispute consultation?
A: 1) Original or certified chain of Title Deeds (Dalil); 2) CS, RS, and latest LR Record of Rights (Porcha/Khatiyan); 3) Up-to-date BL&LRO Land Revenue (Khazna) receipts; 4) Prior plaints, written statements, or judgments (if litigation is pending); 5) Demarcation sketch or sanctioned site plan.

Q: How can I stop unauthorized construction on ancestral land?
A: An urgent application under Order 39 Rules 1 and 2 read with Section 151 CPC must be filed before the competent Civil Court seeking an ad-interim temporary injunction to restrain third-party construction and maintain the status quo. If police assistance is denied despite a court injunction order, an application under Section 151 CPC or an Article 226 Writ Petition before the High Court can be moved.
